question: Islamism poses a threat to our open society and to liberal democracy. The Group of the Greens in the European Parliament is therefore opposed to Islamism. Islamic organisations which undermine democratic institutions and minority rights need to be tackled with decisive action, such as effective investigations, funding transparency and tough law enforcement.

Yet the fight against Islamism must not place Muslims under general suspicion. Parliament’s most recent resolution on Islamism mentions anti-discrimination and pro-equality work several times in connection with Islamism. 1.
What specific measures is the Commission considering to combat Islamism and Islamic terror?

How is it making sure that neither Muslims nor civil society organisations championing diversity and equality and speaking out against discrimination are placed under blanket suspicion as a result of anti-Islamism measures?
In the Commission’s view, to what extent might adding individuals or organisations with links to the Muslim Brotherhood to the EU terror list help combat Islamism?
